title: Hartogs' lemma: for every set A there is an ordinal not injecting into A

statement_spans.label: author lem environment with its own label HartogsLemma (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 674-676

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lem: Pairs (B,R) with B a subset of A and R a well-ordering of B all live in a bounded rank stage V of rank(A)+5 by the rank computation lemma; Separation forms the set C of such well-orderings, Replacement and the ordinal representation theorem collect their order types into a set alpha, transitivity of alpha makes it an ordinal, and a reductio shows no injection from alpha into A exists. (source lines 678-707)

standard_prerequisites.name: Rank computation for subsets and products (set-theory-ord-arithmetic chapter, Lemma rankcomputation, source line 820)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the rank bound placing every pair (B,R) with B a subset of A and R a subset of the square of B inside the stage V of rank(A)+4.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ordinal representation theorem (set-theory-ordinals chapter, Theorem thmOrdinalRepresentation, source line 1020)
standard_prerequisites.use: Guarantees each well-ordering (B,R) has an order type, so Replacement can collect the order types of C into a set.

standard_prerequisites.name: Corollary: a transitive set of ordinals is an ordinal (set-theory-ordinals chapter, Corollary corordtransitiveord, source line 534)
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the collected set alpha as an ordinal once transitivity is checked.

standard_prerequisites.name: Initial segments of well-orderings (set-theory-ordinals chapter, Lemma wellordinitialsegment, source line 799)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows predecessors gamma of an order type are themselves order types of initial segments, which is what makes alpha transitive.

core_obligations: Establish the rank bound (proof lines 679-681): for B a subset of A and R a subset of the square of B, the pair (B,R) lies in the stage V of rank(A)+4, citing the rank computation lemma; hence Separation over the stage of rank(A)+5 collects C, the set of pairs (B,R) in that stage with B a subset of A and (B,R) a well-ordering (proof lines 682-686).
Collect the order types (proof lines 687-691): by Replacement and the ordinal representation theorem, alpha = { type(B,R) : (B,R) in C } is a set.

Show alpha is an ordinal (proof lines 692-697): if gamma is in beta is in alpha then beta = type(B,R) for some member and gamma = type of an initial segment of (B,R) by wellordinitialsegment, so gamma is in alpha; alpha is transitive, hence an ordinal by corordtransitiveord.

Prove no injection from alpha into A exists (proof lines 699-706): if f were such an injection, its range B with the pushed-forward order R would satisfy type(B,R) = alpha and (B,R) in C, whence alpha in alpha, contradicting the irreflexivity of ordinals.
proof_roadmap: Bound the rank of candidate well-orderings and collect them by Separation (proof lines 679-686).
Collect order types by Replacement and the representation theorem (proof lines 687-691).
Prove transitivity of the collected set, hence it is an ordinal (proof lines 692-697).
Reductio with the range of a would-be injection (proof lines 699-706).
difficulty_reason: The Hartogs construction: bounded-rank Separation plus Replacement collecting order types, a transitivity check driven by initial segments, and a reductio; four named cross-chapter citations, 30-line proof, the construction is written out in full.
